notes: Event date: 25 November 1944 (Wikipedia; CMH Riviera to the Rhine, p. 419). Event definition: Under General Carpentier the division pierces the German position in the Belfort Gap on 14 November, seizes Montbeliard and Hericourt and enters Belfort on 25 November, with combat command CC6 of the 5th Armored Division attached. Event support: two source families (Wikipedia and the US Army official history (CMH)), and de Lattre's History of the French First Army, which disagrees on the date. Wikipedia, 2nd Moroccan Infantry Division, section French & German campaign (1944-1945): "it was positioned opposite the Belfort gap, pierced the German position on November 14, seized Montbéliard and Héricourt, and entered Belfort on November 25"; CMH Riviera to the Rhine ch. 23 p. 419: "In fact, the 2d Moroccan Division, even with the support of CC6, was unable to clear the Belfort area until 25 November"; de Lattre, The History of the French First Army (1952) p. 243-246: "They only surrendered on the 21st, when Belfort had fallen.". Location: Belfort, Territoire de Belfort with a precision of 5 km. Location support: Wikipedia names Belfort and the CMH history the Belfort area, both for 25 November and the division: two source families for an area-level place, so 0.7. French follow-up: confidence raised from 0.5 to 0.7 after the CMH history (p. 419) was read as a second source family. Commander: General Marcel Carpentier commands the division, September 1944 to April 1945 (Wikipedia). Review (French follow-up, de Lattre): de Lattre (pp. 243-246), in the pages on the 2nd DIM (8th and 4th RTM) in the Belfort woods and forts, says the forts surrendered on 21 November "when Belfort had fallen", four days before the 25 November of Wikipedia and the CMH history (which says the division could not clear the Belfort area until 25 November). The two can be read as the town (21 November) and the whole area (25 November); not reconciled, so the row keeps 25 November and 0.7.
